newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's AMP sees capital at A$8-10 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's AMP sees capital at A$8-10 bln.

text.p: The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Thursday it saw member's capital at A$8 to A$10 billion in 1998 and had an open mind on raising capital when it floated following a proposed demutualisation.

The company earlier announced it would recommend to members that it demutualise with a listing on the Australian Stock Exchange in mid-to-late 1998. "We'd see member's capital in the range of A$8 to A$10 billion in 1998 when we plan to list," managing director George Trumbull told a news conference when asked what market capitalisation would be.
Trumbull said he saw AMP as being among the top 10 Australian listed stocks but that he could not predict the market capitalisation when it floated.
He said AMP had no great need at present to raise capital because it was well capitalised, but that he had an open mind about a possible capital raising along with the float.
Such a decision would depend on the economics of using the sharemarket to raise capital, he said.
AMP would look at listing in Australia and New Zealand and possibly in the United Kingdom.
AMP has about A$90 billion of assets and is the largest investor in the Australian share market, as well as being the country's largest insurer.
